newsitem.title: FRANCE: France warns of grain damage from dry weather.
newsitem.headline: France warns of grain damage from dry weather.

text.p: The French farm ministry added its own voice on Monday to early predictions of drought with a warning that winter cereals and rapeseed crops could be damaged if there is no break in the weather soon.
The ministry's SCEES statistical office, in a report on sowing estimates for the 1997 harvest, said some parts of France had seen no rain last month and this could hit crop development.
"This situation, while allowing spring crops to become planted, could eventually penalise the development and the potential of winter cereals and rapeseed crops," it said.
It did give a figure for potential yield losses.
Ministry figures show eight millimetres of rainfall in grain-rich central and eastern France in March, 51 millimetres below the 30-year base average between 1951 and 1980.
Southeastern France had just one millimetre of rain while the wettest area was northeastern France with 20 millimetres -- still 32 millimetres below the region's average.
"Rainfall in March was very poor," SCEES said in a statement.

"Precipitation was well below normal in northern France, the north of the Paris basin and the northeast, and was practically absent everywhere else, with variations of 85 percent, 95 percent or even 100 percent below normal in the southeast."

Grain producing organisations and weather forecasters have warned of damage to yields if the weather stays dry for several weeks. But they caution that similar predictions during a dry spell last year were eventually swept aside by a record crop.
Weighing against any loss in yields, the farm ministry said on Monday the area sown to winter wheat and barley had risen this year while winter durum and oat sowings were down.
Winter soft wheat sowings are up 3.4 percent, barley up 4.9 percent, durum down 4.5 percent and oats down 14.7 percent.
Winter rapeseed sowings rose 8.2 percent, the report said, based on estimates effective April 1.
